outline:
This course introduces the methods and applications of data mining.
The topics include data management, data mining techniques, big data platforms, and project implementation and presentation.
Students are expected to learn the concepts and techniques of data mining algorithms, and their applications and future trends in different case studies.
schedule:
Part I: Data mining concepts (7 wks)
1. Introduction to data mining & data preprocessing (1 wk)
2. Frequent pattern mining (2 wks)
3. Data classification (2 wks)
4. Data clustering (1 wk)
5. Midterm exam (1 wk)

Part II: Distributed processing (5 wks)

1. Introduction to distributed platforms: Hadoop & Spark (1 wk)
2. MapReduce programming: relational algebra, pairs & stripes (1 wk)
3. Case study of Spark programming: frequent itemset, classification, clustering (2 wks)
4. Term Project presentation (1 wk)
scorePolicy:
Homework assignments and programming exercises: ~30-35%
Mid-term exam: ~30-35%
Term Project: ~30-35%
materials:
- Textbook:
Jiawei Han, Micheline Kamber, and Jian Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, 3rd edition, Morgan Kaufmann, 2011.

- References:
1. Jimmy Lin and Chris Dyer, Data-Intensive Text Processing with MapReduce,
Morgan & Claypool Publishers, 2010.
2. Holden Karau, andy Konwinski, Patrick Wendell, and Matei Zaharia, Learning Spark: Lightning-fast data analysis, O'Reilly, 2015.
3. Recent academic papers, tutorials, and slides.

- Latest news available soon at: https://chriswjh.github.io/DM/
consultation:
The teacher can be reached via e-mails or messages in Microsoft Teams.
The TA will help you join the course group in Facebook
where you can also ask questions about the homeworks and exams.
remarks:
All course sessions will be recorded and put on iSchool+ afterwards, along with all course materials, homework announcements and submissions.
To prepare for further impacts of COVID-19 pandemic, the following channels will be set up:
1. Microsoft Teams: you will be automatically added to the team for your enrolled courses in Teams. When the course is held online, please join our class with your Teams ID (StudentID@cc.ntut.edu.tw).
2. Facebook: we will set up a group for the course in Facebook
where you can also ask questions about the homeworks and exams.
